newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dollar to pale versus rising yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dollar to pale versus rising yen.

text.p: The dollar, after violating rising trendlines versus the mark, seems to have nowhere to go but lower while the yen should rise and shine again, chartists said on Monday.

At 1800 EDT/2130 GMT, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7172/77 versus 1.7210/20 at the open and 1.7285/90 at the close on Friday. Meanwhile, dollar/yen traded at 114.74/79 vs. 115.30/40 at the open and 114.80/90 at the prior close.
"The dollar does not look good. Dollar/yen stopped right below the 115.70 resistance level," said analyst Ben Morden at I.D.E.A.
Morden said 115.70, the June 12 high, may be a temporary top for dollar/yen, which faltered at an intraday high of 115.67 on Monday.
"The risk for dollar/yen now is a retreat to 114.25. We could get some support there, and go back up to the 115.50 area. That should be the range short term," Morden predicted.

Chartists agreed that 117.00, the dollar/yen recent peak set on May 28, is clearly out of reach over the coming sessions. That level also is a 38-percent Fibonacci retracement of the broader dollar/yen range from a high of 127.47 on May 1 to a low of 110.62 on June 11.
If 114.25/30 level gives way, the next supports are seen at 114 yen, and 113.75.
"The yen will be the next leader," Morden predicted.
Turning to dollar/mark, Morden pointed out that it "broke the low end of a two-week rising channel at 1.7185, and it broke a six-week rising trendline in the 1.7240/60 area."
Morden stressed "the risk now is 1.7020. No matter what you are looking at, the charts are pointing down."
Chartists agreed that dollar/mark likely topped out just above 1.74, after peaking at 1.7423 on June 6 -- a 39-month high -- and at 1.7407 on June 13.

Meanwhile, cable convincingly took out a key level on a four-month rising trendline at $1.666. However, cable soon ran out of steam after a brief foray above $1.67 that ended short of $1.6735 resistance, chartists said.
Also, sterling/mark may be topping out at 2.87, below a target at 2.8735, they added.
In another sign of weakness for the U.S. currency, dollar/Swiss set lower highs, in tandem with dollar/mark.
The loss of 1.4255, a 50-percent retracement of the rise from 1.3880, the May 26 low, to 1.4625, the June 6 high, would be clearly bearish, analysts said.
